title.narrative: Sustainable Livestock in the forest region of the Argentine Parque ChaqueÃ±o through Forest Management with Integrated Livestock (MBGI)

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project's benefits are expected to improve livestock management in forest environments, improving the protection of biodiversity and the livelihoods of primary producers and members of the beef value chain in at least 14 departments in four provinces of the RFPCh. More employment opportunities will be generated, and employment conditions will be improved by promoting decent employment and continuous improvements in working conditions, avoiding conditions that promote migration and uprooting. The project will contribute to improving environmental protection and the sustainable use of its components in areas under MBGI improving competitiveness in markets calling for specific traceability (environmental, social, health), as well as reducing pollution due to less and efficient use of agrochemicals. These changes will contribute to generating global environmental benefits by increasing the area under improved practices to favour biodiversity, through MBGI (maintain and increase biodiversity reservoirs in production areas), and reducing emissions from land use both at the production level and throughout the supply chain. Regarding equality between men and women, since the project is targeted to medium and large producers, it will carry out a diagnostic study to address existing gaps in accessing resources, decision-making and sharing of benefits, also including elements from all the chain’s links. The strengthening and updating of MBGI governance, which considers three interrelated management scales (1) at the landscape level; (2) at the farm level; and (3) at the landscape unit or grove level, and the replacement of Traditional Silvo-pastoral Systems (SSPT), contributes to resilient management at the landscape level. In addition, it also contributes to strengthening governance and obtaining local and global environmental benefits: (i) integration throughout the MBGI-CVCV, identification and integration of risks (agro-climate, market, etc.) into informed decision-making; (ii) improvement and updating of social-environmental information and monitoring systems, through multi-level participation mechanisms and transparency from production to consumption; (iii) the integration of knowledge management throughout the MBGI-CVCV.

To achieve biodiversity conservation of the Parque ChaqueÃ±o Forest Region by promoting MBGI among medium to large-sized livestock producers in native forests under three-fold impact schemes (that include strengthened capacities, incentives mechanisms and improved governance) in 14 departments in the provinces of Salta, Santiago del Estero, Chaco and Formosa.
